message.content: {"reading": {"line": "Stoic freedom depends on seeing the limits of your power, not on changing the world.", "options": [{"move": "the older version", "note": "Epictetus’s dichotomy of control refines a theme from earlier Cynic philosophy, which also urged indifference to externals but lacked the Stoic distinction between what is and isn’t up to us."}, {"move": "the sharper version", "note": "Taken strictly, the dichotomy of control means that any effort to change external events for their own sake is a distraction from freedom itself."}, {"move": "the test", "note": "If Stoic freedom works, then people who accept the limits of their control should show less distress in the face of setbacks than those who try to control everything."}], "pick": 0}, "insights": [{"index": 0, "move": "first of its kind", "headline": "No other save yet claims that freedom is a matter of judgment rather than control."}]}
